snippet.title: Creating the first open-world chess | ChessWorlds
snippet.description:
Try the game on Itch: https://firststef.itch.io/chessworlds
Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/4922520/ChessWorlds

ChessWorlds is a 3D tactics game where chess pieces climb terrain, drop off ledges, and fight across a board with real height.

It is a single-player tactics game, every piece keeps its chess range but the battlefield has height, so pieces climb up one tile to reach a square, the knight jumps two. The pawn even gets its moveset mirrored to every direction, because on a 3D board you can face any way.

You play a king whose kingdom fell in a single night, and you travel out to reclaim it across four realms that each break chess in their own way: the elves who hide in cover and strike from range, the dwarves who shove you off ledges, the mermaids who flood the board, and the constructs who stack on top of each other and stack actions that fire turns later.

And you can design your own pieces. The Piece Designer is a visual, block-based workshop, and "See it in action" drops your creation straight into a test battle.

Honest framing: this is an early playtest, not a demo and not a finished release. It is rough and there are bugs, and that is exactly why it is out. I want to know what is broken, what is confusing, and what is fun.

LINKS
- Discord (talk to me, give feedback): https://discord.gg/ZhkX3DYhZh
- Free demo on itch: https://firststef.itch.io/chessworlds
- Patreon (Workshop Edition = the Piece Designer): https://www.patreon.com/firststef/posts/chess-worlds-163086668
